notes: DRAFT, refused by the engine -- kept as the record of the refusal (teaching-note.md), the matrix's flawed-example row for T-15. At the 2026-07-28 huddle, with the engine Pareto on the table, the two vital-few causes were marked verified on the spot -- 'the Pareto already proved it, the whole room agrees' -- with their evidence fields left empty and the why-chains still unbuilt. The schema itself is the gate (R-ANA-02's anchor line: team consensus is not evidence): status='verified' cannot be constructed without a non-empty evidence object, so POST /artifacts/T-15/validate came back 422 naming each consensus-verified cause, before any prescore ran. The corrected board (fishbone-corrected.json, saved the same afternoon as print-fishbone v1) attaches the pointers the huddle already had -- the check sheet's transcribed tally, the Pareto's own dataset export -- and does the verification work these statuses were only claiming: the prepress walk and the traveler audit that become the 5-Why chain.

effect.text: 8.6% of orders fail the customer's first look at the QC desk (135 of 1,566 in the 21-day baseline census, p-bar 0.086207 frozen and stable) -- the charter's baselined problem, tracked as the daily rejected proportion

causes.text: Jobs reach the cutter without a signed-off imposition -- fold and bleed get set per operator habit at prepress, so trim registration drifts from job to job
Paper trays get reloaded between jobs with unlabeled stock, so the press pulls whatever sheet is in the tray when the SKU changes mid-shift
Smudge and banding marks cluster on rush jobs racked before full ink cure
Wrong-quantity orders trace to counting by lift thickness at the cutter instead of running the sheet counter on mixed-stock jobs
